I am available on Monday and Wednesday afternoons after 1 p.m., and I could also come in on Friday morning. I am happy to adjust my schedule to whatever works best for you or the lab assistant.

Thank you very much for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Anna

Warm regards,
Priyanka

Dear Dr. Kim,

I am a third-year environmental science student at Northfield University, and I am writing about my registration for the regional student conference next month. I registered through the conference website on September 2, filled in all the required information, and paid the $40 student fee by credit card.

However, I have not received a confirmation email. I have checked my spam and junk folders several times, and when I log in to the website, it does not show any record of my registration. My bank statement does show the payment, so I am unsure whether the registration was completed correctly.

Since the conference is only three weeks away and I need to book my travel and accommodation soon, could you please confirm whether I am registered? If something went wrong, I would be happy to register again or send a copy of my payment receipt.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Oliver

Hi Leo,

It was great to hear from you, though I'm sorry you've been feeling lonely. That's completely normal when you move somewhere new. I felt exactly the same way during my first two months there, so please don't be too hard on yourself. It does get better!

There are a couple of places you should definitely check out. First, go to Harbor Market on a Saturday morning. It's full of food stalls and local musicians, and it's the perfect place to wander around. Second, try Riverside Park, which has great walking trails and a small café by the water. I used to read there every Sunday afternoon.

As for meeting people, I really recommend joining the running club that meets at the park on Wednesday evenings. Everyone is friendly, and they usually go out for pizza afterward. That's actually how I met most of my friends in the city.

Keep me updated, and call me anytime!

Take care,
Maya

Sincerely,
Jenna

Dear Mr. Fischer,

I am writing about the laundry machines in the basement of our building. All three washers and both dryers have been out of order for ten days now. Each one has an "Out of Service" sign on it, but no notice has been posted explaining what happened or when they will be fixed.

This has been very inconvenient for everyone. Since I don't have a car, I have had to carry heavy bags of clothes on the bus to a laundromat across town, which takes almost three hours each time. Several neighbors, including an elderly couple on the second floor, have told me they are struggling with the same problem.

Could you please tell us when the machines are expected to be repaired? In the meantime, would it be possible to arrange a temporary solution, such as a discount at the nearest laundromat or a weekly laundry pickup service paid for by the building?

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
Adrian

Dear Ms. Grant,

I hope you are doing well. In addition to working at the dining hall, I am a member of the student volunteer committee, which is organizing a campus food drive from November 3 to 14. Our goal is to collect 2,000 cans and boxes of non-perishable food for the Eastside Community Food Bank, which supports more than 300 local families.

Since so many students pass through the dining hall every day, it would be the perfect place to collect donations. We would like to place one large donation box near the main entrance, next to the menu board, where it would be visible but would not block the line. We would also appreciate permission to hang a small poster about the drive.

Our committee will take full responsibility for the box. Two volunteers will empty it every evening, store the donations in the student center, and deliver everything to the food bank at the end of each week.

Thank you for considering our request.

Best regards,
Nina

Dear Mr. Nguyen,

Most afternoons, from around 1 p.m. until 5 p.m., your dog Max barks quite loudly, sometimes for long stretches without stopping. I think he may just be lonely while you are away.

I study at home in the afternoons, and I have been finding it difficult to concentrate, especially now that I am preparing for my final exams. I have tried wearing headphones, but the barking still comes through clearly.

I was wondering if we could find a solution that works for both of us. Perhaps a dog walker could take Max out in the early afternoon, or he could have a few chew toys to keep him busy. If it would help, I would also be happy to walk him myself once or twice a week, since I really like him.

Thank you for understanding.

Best wishes,
Claire

Thank you for understanding.

Best wishes,
Claire

Your collection of nineteenth-century port maps is the only one in the region that covers this period in detail, so examining the originals is essential to my research. Unfortunately, the digital copies do not show the handwritten notes in the margins, which are central to my argument.

My difficulty is one of timing. As part of my degree, I am completing a required internship at the Maritime Heritage Museum from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. every weekday this semester. Because special collections is open only on weekday mornings, I have not been able to visit at all.

Would it be possible to arrange supervised access on two afternoons per month? I would be happy to work during a staff member's regular hours, follow all handling rules, and request specific maps a week in advance so they could be prepared beforehand.

Thank you for considering this request.

Sincerely,
Isabel

Dear Coach Abara,

Thank you for asking for our feedback on the new training schedule. I can already see some benefits: our fitness has clearly improved, and the extra sessions have given us more time to work on set pieces, which helped us beat Eastfield last week.

However, several teammates and I have some concerns. Because the morning sessions start at 6 a.m. three days a week, many of us are getting only five or six hours of sleep. We feel exhausted in afternoon classes, and a few players say their grades are slipping. More worrying, we've had four minor injuries in the past month, compared with one in the entire previous season, and I suspect fatigue is a factor.

I'd like to suggest reducing the early sessions to two days a week and making one of them a lighter recovery session focused on stretching and tactics. That way, we would keep most of the fitness gains while giving our bodies time to recover, which should mean fewer injuries and a stronger squad for the playoffs.

Respectfully,
Tyler

Dear Dr. Feldman,

Thank you for organizing such a well-run conference last weekend. The keynote on coastal ecosystems was inspiring, the sessions ran on time, and the networking lunch gave me the chance to meet researchers I had only read about.

I would, however, like to comment on the poster session. The posters were placed in the narrow hallway behind registration, which most attendees passed only on their way to the restrooms. Because the session also overlapped with two popular talks, very few people came by. In ninety minutes, I spoke with only three visitors, and the presenter next to me had none at all.

For next year, I would suggest holding the poster session in a central space, such as the main lobby, at a time when no talks are scheduled. Serving coffee nearby would also encourage people to stay. Finally, a short preview session in which each presenter gives a one-minute summary would help attract an audience.

Best regards,
Min-jun

Thank you very much for your time.

Sincerely,
Arjun Mehta

Dear Mr. Castillo,

I received your notice about the fifteen percent rent increase beginning next month, and I am writing to share a concern. According to Section 7 of our lease, any change to the rent requires at least sixty days' written notice. Since the notice was delivered on March 15, I believe the increase cannot take effect before mid-May.

Beyond the timing, an increase of this size would be very difficult for me. My rent would rise by $210 a month, which is more than my entire monthly grocery budget. I would have to move out, even though I would much prefer to stay.

Over the past two years, I have paid on time every month and taken good care of the unit. With that in mind, I would like to propose a compromise: an increase of eight percent starting in mid-May, in line with the required notice period, with a further review when the lease is renewed next year.

I hope we can find an arrangement that works for both of us.

Sincerely,
Grace Liu

Dear Amira,

Thank you for telling me honestly how my comment at last week's practice tournament affected people. I owe you, and especially Daniel, an apology. When I called his argument "obviously naive" in front of the whole room, I was dismissive and disrespectful, and there is no excuse for that. I have also apologized to him personally.

Looking back, I realize I was so focused on winning the round that I forgot the purpose of a practice tournament. It is supposed to be a place where members, especially newer ones, can take risks and test ideas without fear of being mocked. A good debater challenges arguments, not people, and I failed to do that.

To help make the club more respectful, I would like to suggest that we agree on a short code of conduct at the next meeting, including a rule about criticizing ideas rather than individuals. I would also be glad to lead a brief workshop on giving constructive feedback, since I clearly need the practice myself.

Sincerely,
Owen

Dear Ms. Lindqvist,

Thank you for asking us for ideas about attracting younger customers. I have one that I think could work well.

Over the past few months, I've noticed that the café next door is full of students every afternoon and evening, studying for hours. Many of them pass our window, but very few come inside, perhaps because they see bookstores as places to browse quickly rather than to spend time.

My proposal is a weekly "Study Night" every Wednesday from 6 to 9 p.m. We could set up a few tables in the back corner, offer free Wi-Fi, and give attendees ten percent off study guides and novels. Once a month, a local author could give a short talk.

The store would benefit by turning those café visitors into regular customers who discover our books while they are already here. The costs would be modest: a few folding tables, some posters for nearby campuses, and one extra staff member during those hours, a shift I would be happy to cover.

Best regards,
Lucas

Dear Mr. and Mrs. Okonkwo,

Welcome to Linden Road! My name is Clara, and I live in the yellow house right next door. I hope the move went smoothly and that you're starting to feel settled. Please don't hesitate to knock if you ever need anything.

I'm also writing to tell you about our community garden day, which takes place every spring. This year, it will be held on Saturday, April 20, from 9 a.m. to noon in the small park at the end of the street. Neighbors work together to plant flowers, clean up the paths, and build new vegetable beds. Really, it's a chance to get to know one another, and we always finish with a potluck lunch.

You'd be very welcome to join us, even for just an hour. There are tasks for every age and energy level, from planting to painting signs with the children or simply bringing a dish to share. Of course, there's no obligation at all; I just wanted you to know you're invited.

Warm regards,
Clara

Sincerely,
Martin Kovač

I can think of a few possible solutions. Ideally, I could present at any time on the second or third day. If that is not possible, I would be glad to exchange slots with another presenter, or, as a last resort, give my talk remotely by video. I would prefer the first option, since presenting in person would allow me to discuss my work with other researchers more fully.

Thank you for your understanding.

Best regards,
Amara Singh

Dear Ms. Jennings,

I am a resident on the third floor of Maple Hall, and I am writing about the renovation work next door at Carver Hall. Since last Monday, the crews have been using jackhammers and a concrete mixer starting at exactly 7 a.m., and the noise continues almost without a break until late afternoon. Even with my windows closed, it sounds as though the work is happening inside my room.

The timing is especially difficult because final exams begin in ten days. Many of us study until midnight or later, so we are losing several hours of sleep every morning. Two of my neighbors have even started going to the library at dawn just to escape the noise.

I understand that the renovation needs to be finished, but could your office ask the contractor to start at 9 a.m. during the exam period? If that is not possible, perhaps the university could open a quiet study room for residents in the mornings.

Thank you for considering this.

Sincerely,
Aisha

If you sign up, I still have my old workshop notes and the reading list. I'd be glad to lend them to you before the semester starts.

Cheers,
Noah

Dear Mr. Ellis,

I saw the notice inviting suggestions for the student union, and I would like to share an idea about the second-floor study lounge. I spend about two hours there almost every day between classes. It is bright, comfortable, and close to my lecture halls, so it has become my favorite place on campus to review notes and finish assignments.

Unfortunately, the lounge has only six electrical outlets, and they are all along one wall. By midmorning, every outlet is taken, so students end up sitting on the floor with their laptops just to stay charged. Others simply leave when their batteries run low, which seems like a waste of such a pleasant space.

I would suggest installing charging stations on the large tables in the middle of the room, or at least adding a few secured power strips there. The engineering library already has tables with built-in outlets, and students use them constantly.

Thank you for considering this idea.

Sincerely,
Julia

Lucas

Dear Transportation Services,

I am writing about a problem with the evening Green Line shuttle at the Science Library stop. Three times in the past two weeks, most recently last Wednesday, the 9:10 p.m. shuttle drove past the stop without slowing down, even though I was standing right next to the sign. On two of those nights, another student was waiting with me.

Because the next shuttle does not arrive until 9:50, I have had to wait alone in the dark for forty minutes. The area around the library is very quiet at night, and I honestly do not feel safe there. Missing the shuttle also means I get home late and have less time to prepare for my early classes.

Perhaps drivers on the evening route could be reminded to stop at every posted stop after dark, even if they cannot see anyone. Another option would be better lighting at the stop so that drivers can easily see waiting passengers.

Thank you for looking into this.

Sincerely,
Grace

Hi Jacob,

I'm really sorry, but I have some bad news about your biology textbook. Yesterday evening I was studying at my desk, and when I reached for my notebook, I knocked over a full cup of coffee. Most of it landed on the book before I could grab it. I feel terrible, especially because you were so generous to lend it to me.

The cover is fine, but about twenty pages in Chapter 6 are stained brown and a little wrinkled. The text is still readable, but the pages stick together slightly, and the diagrams on cellular respiration are harder to see.

A survey I conducted through the International Student Association last month found that almost 60 percent of first-year international students have no close local friends, and many said they feel isolated on weekends.

To address this, I would like to start a program called Coffee Partners. Each international student would be matched with a local volunteer, and the pairs would meet for coffee once a week to practice conversation and share their cultures. Once a month, all participants would gather for a larger social event, such as a potluck or a game night.

To launch the program, I would need about $800 for coffee vouchers and monthly events, as well as help advertising through the student government's social media accounts. I would be happy to present a detailed plan at your next meeting.

Best regards,
Minh

I understand that the university is facing a serious housing shortage, and I appreciate how difficult it must be to find space for everyone. Nevertheless, I am very concerned about this change.

When I shared a room during my first year, my symptoms returned and my grades suffered. Because the single room is an approved accommodation rather than a preference, I hope the decision can be reconsidered.

If keeping my current room is impossible, could I be offered a single room in another building, even a smaller one? I would also be willing to move into a university apartment off campus if one becomes available.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Sophie

transcription.text:
Dear Dr. Monroe,

Thank you for your letter about my Founders' Merit Scholarship. I am writing to appeal the decision and to ask the committee to consider the circumstances behind my lower GPA.

In the middle of last semester, I was diagnosed with mononucleosis and spent nearly six weeks with extreme fatigue. I tried to keep attending classes, but I missed several exams and had to take them late, often while still ill. As a result, my GPA fell from 3.7 to 3.3, the first time it has ever dropped below the requirement.

Since recovering, I have worked hard to get back on track. I meet weekly with a tutor in organic chemistry, I have reduced my hours at my campus job, and my midterm grades this semester are all A's and B+'s.

I would be very grateful if the committee allowed me one probationary semester to raise my GPA. My record before my illness shows what I am capable of, and this scholarship is what makes it possible for me to stay at the university.

Respectfully,
Andre

Hi Zoe,

Thanks for explaining the new membership fee at Tuesday's meeting. I completely agree that our tents and stoves need replacing. Two of the tents leaked badly on the October trip, and it's clear we can't keep running safe trips with old equipment. I appreciate that you're taking the problem seriously.

That said, I'm worried that raising dues from $20 to $75 could push some people out. Several members, especially first-years and students who pay their own tuition, have told me privately that they might not renew. Since the club has always prided itself on making the outdoors accessible to everyone, losing them would be a real loss.

Would you consider a different approach? We could raise the regular fee to $30 and offer an optional "supporter" membership for those who can pay more. We could also hold a gear swap as a fundraiser and apply for a grant from the student activities office. I'd be glad to help organize either one.

Best,
Owen

Hey Ben,

The thing that's been bothering me is the late nights. Over the last month, your friends have been staying over three or four nights a week, and the games in the living room often go until 2 a.m. My room is right next to it, and since I have 8 a.m. classes four days a week, I've been running on about five hours of sleep. I'm not upset with anyone; I just hadn't said anything until now.

Would you be open to keeping things quiet after midnight on weeknights? Weekends would be totally fine for later nights. Maybe we could also give each other a heads-up when guests are staying over.

Let me know what you think.

Thanks,
Tom

Dear Professor Weiss,

Thank you so much for inviting me to join your lab next year. Your Cognitive Neuroscience course was the highlight of my sophomore year, and being asked to work with you is one of the greatest compliments I have received as a student. I thought about your offer for several days before writing back.

Unfortunately, I must decline. Two weeks ago, before your offer arrived, I accepted a position in Dr. Ramos's lab, where I will help study language development in bilingual children. Since I plan to apply to graduate programs in developmental psychology, the project fits my long-term goals closely, and I did not feel it would be fair to withdraw from a commitment I had already made.

I would still love to stay connected to your work. Would it be possible for me to attend your lab's monthly journal club as a guest? I am also planning to take your seminar on memory next fall.

Thank you again for your confidence in me.

Warm regards,
Irene

Benjamin

Dear Dr. Shaw,

I am a student in Introductory Biology, and I would like to raise a concern about lab report grading on behalf of several classmates. After the second lab, a group of us from four different sections compared our reports. We found that reports with nearly identical data and analysis received very different scores. In one case, two students with almost the same discussion section received 92 and 74 points.

I want to be clear that I am not criticizing any individual teaching assistant; all of them have been helpful and hardworking. Still, because lab reports make up 25 percent of our final grade, these differences could affect students' GPAs and, for pre-medical students, even their applications.

One solution might be a detailed common rubric, shared with students before each lab, that lists point values for every part of the report. It could also help if the teaching assistants graded a few sample reports together at the start of the semester to agree on standards.

Thank you for considering this.

Sincerely,
Lena

Starting on March 4, I will be teaching free swimming lessons to children at the Riverside Community Pool every Saturday from 8 a.m. to noon, which directly overlaps with my current hours.

If you approve this change, I would be glad to work both shifts during the first week so that Dana and I can make sure nothing is missed. I could also update the shift notes for her. Please let me know if you would like to discuss this in person.

Best regards,
Jamal

We meet every Thursday from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Members spend the first half of each session speaking one language and the second half speaking the other, and we sometimes play vocabulary games or discuss short news articles.

Thank you very much for your help.

Kind regards,
Hana

Dear Mr. Hughes,

I hope your tomatoes survived the heat wave better than ours did! I'm writing because I've noticed a problem with the shared plants near the garden entrance. During the last two weeks of hot weather, the basil, mint, and rosemary there turned brown and dry. I think each of us assumed someone else was watering them, so in the end nobody did.

I'd like to suggest a simple rotating schedule. Each member could sign up for one day a week to water the shared beds, and we could post the list on the tool shed door along with a short checklist. With around thirty members, nobody would need to volunteer more than once or twice a month.

If you like this idea, I'd be happy to create the schedule and send a sign-up message to everyone on the email list. I could also replant the herbs this weekend.

Thanks for all the work you do for the garden.

Best wishes,
Nadia

I'm afraid it was my fault. More people came to the party than I had expected, and the street filled up quickly. I should have told everyone where to park, but I was busy in the kitchen and didn't check outside. Two friends who had never visited before simply didn't notice your driveway in the dark.

In the future, I will ask guests to park in the lot behind the pharmacy on Grove Street, and I'll go outside myself to check the street during any gathering. I'll also let you know in advance whenever I'm expecting visitors.

Again, I'm truly sorry. I hope you'll accept a small apple pie as a peace offering this weekend.

Warm regards,
Daniel

Congratulations on getting two job offers! That's impressive, and it's great that you're thinking carefully before choosing. I'm glad you asked me, because I faced almost the same decision when I was your age.

Honestly, I'd go with the camp counselor job. One tip from my own summer at Pine Lake Camp: bring more energy than you think you'll need, and don't be afraid to ask the older counselors for help. The first week was exhausting, and I almost quit, but by the end I didn't want to leave.

Whatever you decide, let me know how it goes!

Talk soon,
Andrea

Dear Ms. Price,

Thank you for the chance to share my thoughts on the adult beginner swimming course, which I completed last week. Overall, it was a wonderful experience. Our instructor, Mr. Alvarez, was patient and encouraging, and he gave each of us individual advice. When I started, I could barely float, but now I can swim two full lengths of the pool without stopping.

However, there was one problem that affected almost every session. Because our class took place during open swim hours, the pool was often crowded, and we were usually given just one narrow lane. Several times we had to wait at the wall for minutes before we could practice.

For future courses, I would suggest scheduling the class at a quieter time, such as early on weekday evenings, or reserving at least two lanes for the group. Even a rope to separate the class area would make a big difference.

Best regards,
Grace

Thank you for your time.

Best,
Jonah

Thank you so much for welcoming me into your home last weekend. From the moment I arrived, you made me feel like part of the family. The guest room was so comfortable that I slept better than I have in months, and I really appreciated you taking the time to show me around.

The highlight of my visit was definitely Saturday afternoon. Walking along the harbor, hearing the story of how the old lighthouse was saved, and then watching the sunset from the hill behind your house was unforgettable. Emma has always said her hometown is beautiful, but now I understand what she meant.

I also have a small favor to ask. I haven't stopped thinking about the fish stew you made on Saturday night! Would you be willing to share the recipe? I'd love to cook it for my roommates and tell them where it came from.

Thank you again for your kindness.

Warmest wishes,
Maya

Dear Mr. Banks,

I'm one of the volunteer assistant coaches for the Eastside Hawks, the under-eleven team that practices at Lincoln Gym on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. I'm writing to ask for help with our equipment.

At the moment, we have only six basketballs for fourteen players, and two of them are so worn that they barely bounce. As a result, during dribbling and shooting drills, more than half the kids end up standing in line instead of practicing. Some of the younger players get bored and lose focus, and they don't touch the ball often enough to improve.

Would it be possible for the league to provide eight new youth-size basketballs before the season starts in two weeks? I'll make sure they are labeled with the team name and stored in a locked bin at the gym after every practice. I'll also count them at the end of each session so none go missing.

Thank you for supporting the league.

Best regards,
Ryan

transcription.text:
Dear Ms. Ortiz,

Thank you for inviting residents to share ideas about building a stronger community here. I have one suggestion that I think would be easy and inexpensive.

Over the past few months, I've noticed that many of our neighbors love to read. I often see people with novels on the benches outside, and almost every week there are perfectly good books thrown into the recycling bin. At the same time, the corner of the lobby next to the mailboxes is completely empty.

My idea is to set up a small book swap shelf in that corner. Residents could leave books they've finished and take any that interest them, with no sign-up or fees. I'd be happy to donate a bookcase and about twenty books to get it started, and to tidy the shelf once a week.

I believe it would reduce waste, save people money, and give neighbors a natural reason to chat with each other while checking their mail.

Kind regards,
Tomás

Dear Customer Service Team,

I am writing because my debit card, ending in 4417, has been blocked while I am abroad. Yesterday afternoon, my payment was declined at a supermarket in Lisbon, and a few minutes later an ATM refused to give me cash. When I checked the banking app, I saw a message saying the card had been frozen because of unusual foreign activity.

I can confirm that these transactions were mine. I am in Portugal visiting relatives from June 3 to June 17, and during that time I will be staying in Lisbon and Porto. I forgot to notify the bank about my trip before I left, which I realize may have caused this.

Could you please unblock my card as soon as possible? I have very little cash and depend on the card for daily expenses. I would also be grateful if you could add a travel note to my account for these dates so that the card is not blocked again.

Thank you for your prompt assistance.

Sincerely,
Paulo Mendes

Dear Ms. Ferreira,

Thank you for letting us know about the change to the end-of-summer schedule. I completely understand that this is an exceptionally busy quarter and that asking senior staff to give up an entire afternoon is difficult right now.

Still, I hope you might reconsider canceling the showcase altogether. For the twelve of us, it is the one opportunity to show leaders what we have built over ten weeks, and for interns hoping to return full-time, it is an important chance to be noticed. The company benefits too: last year, two intern prototypes were adopted by the product team after the showcase.

Would a shorter format be possible? Instead of formal presentations, we could hold a one-hour demo session during lunch in the main conference room. Leaders could drop by for as long as they had time, and we interns would handle all of the setup and catering arrangements ourselves.

I would be glad to coordinate the details if this sounds workable.

Best regards,
Kai

I understand that the gym requires thirty days' notice to freeze a membership, and I can see why that policy exists for planned breaks. However, my injury was sudden and completely unexpected, so giving advance notice was impossible. Under the standard rule, I would pay a full month's fee for a facility I physically cannot use. I have been a member for four years without missing a payment, and I hope that history can be taken into account.

Would you consider freezing my membership starting today, for nine weeks? I would be happy to pay the usual freeze fee of $10 per month, and I fully intend to return as soon as I recover.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Natalie

I am very sorry for the error on the flyers for your grand opening. I prepared the order myself, and the incorrect phone number was entirely my mistake. I understand how frustrating this must be, especially since you have already handed out so many of them.

When I typed the text from your order form, I reversed two digits in the number, and I did not ask you to check a final proof before printing. That step is normally part of our process, but because we were very busy that afternoon, I skipped it. I should not have done so.

To fix the problem, we will reprint all 500 flyers with the correct number free of charge, and they will be ready by noon tomorrow. My manager has also agreed to print 200 small correction cards for your counter and to give you 20 percent off your next order. From now on, I will send every customer a proof before printing.

With sincere apologies,
Jordan Lee
Bright Print Shop

I hope you are well. I am writing to request your approval for a short-term sublet of my apartment, unit 12, from June 1 to August 31. I have been offered a paid summer internship at an engineering firm in Denver, and paying rent in two cities for three months would be very difficult for me.

Thank you for considering this.

Sincerely,
Ahmed

transcription.text:
Dear Council Member Rivera,

Thank you for inviting residents to comment on the proposal for Willow Park. As someone who has lived on Birch Street for six years, I would like to share my concerns.

Willow Park is the heart of our neighborhood. I walk there every morning, and on weekends the playground is full of families, while older residents meet on the benches near the fountain. For many people in nearby apartments, it is the only place where they can enjoy trees and fresh air.

Turning half of it into a parking lot would harm the neighborhood in several ways. It would remove the only shaded area during hot summers, increase traffic next to the playground, and leave too little space for the community events held there each year.

I understand that the new shopping center needs parking. However, the empty lot behind the old post office on Fifth Avenue is only two blocks away. Building a parking garage on that site would meet the need without sacrificing our green space.

Respectfully,
Helen Brooks

Hi Omar,

I've been thinking about your message all week, and first of all, I'm honored that you'd want me as a partner. Your falafel wraps are the best I've ever had, and your plan to park near the office buildings at lunchtime and the stadium on game nights is genuinely smart. I have no doubt people will line up for your food.

That's why this has been hard to write. I've decided not to invest or become a partner. As you know, I'm saving for my master's program, which starts next fall, and that $10,000 is a big part of my tuition. If something unexpected happened with the truck, I'd be in a really difficult position, and I'd hate for money to ever come between us.

But I still want to help in any way I can. I could design your logo and menu, set up your social media accounts, and work at the truck on Saturdays during your first month. Just tell me where you need me.

Your friend always,
Sam

Thanks,
Mia

Dear Customer Relations Manager,

I am writing about my recent five-day package to Crete (booking reference SP-58214), from September 3 to 8. I paid $1,850 for a trip that promised accommodation at the Azure Bay Resort, which your brochure describes as a four-star beachfront hotel.

When I arrived, however, I was told I had been moved to the Hotel Kostas, a two-star property twenty minutes from the beach by bus. No one explained the change or apologized. The room was small, the air conditioning was unreliable, and the only restaurant closed at 8 p.m.

As a result, the relaxing beach holiday I had planned for months became a series of bus rides. I also spent about $120 on transportation and meals that would have been included at the original resort.

Since I received a far lower level of service than I paid for, I believe a refund of 40 percent of the package price, plus my additional costs, would be fair. I have kept all receipts and can send them on request.

Sincerely,
Laura Chen

Dear Ms. Wong,

I am writing about the $90 replacement fee on my library account for two books, a cookbook and a travel guide to Japan. On October 2, a pipe burst in the apartment above mine, and water poured through my ceiling overnight. The two library books on my coffee table were soaked and are no longer usable. I have attached a letter from my building manager confirming the incident.

I fully accept that the library should not lose money because of what happened. However, the damage was not caused by any carelessness on my part, and unfortunately, my building's insurance does not cover borrowed items. I have used this library for over ten years and have always returned books on time.

Would it be possible for me to replace the books myself? I have found new copies of both titles online for about $45 in total. Alternatively, I would be glad to pay a reduced fee or to volunteer at the library to cover the difference.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Victor

Best wishes,
Fatima

Whatever you decide, I'm on your side.

Love,
Nora

I hope you and Margaret are enjoying the warmer weather. I wanted to write to you about something I noticed in the backyard, since I think it affects both of us.

After the heavy rain last week, about three meters of the fence between our yards started leaning badly. When I looked more closely, it seemed that the roots of your beautiful oak tree have gradually lifted the posts. Some of the larger branches are also now resting on the edge of my roof.

I'd like to deal with it fairly soon, because the fence could fall during the next storm, and my dog could easily get out into the street. The branches may also damage my gutters.

A contractor I trust estimated $1,200 to replace that section. Since the fence belongs to both of us, would you be willing to split the cost equally? In return, I'd be happy to arrange and pay for trimming the branches over my side. I'm free to talk over coffee anytime this week.

Best,
Simone

Dear Mr. Karimi,

On March 2, your shop replaced the cracked screen on my phone for $160, and the repair came with a 90-day warranty. The screen worked well at first, but last week it began to flicker, and now the bottom third no longer responds to touch. I have not dropped the phone since the repair, and it has always been in a protective case.

When I visited the shop on Monday, your assistant explained that the warranty had expired five days earlier and that he could not help. I understand that warranties need a firm end date. However, a screen that fails after just over three months suggests that the part itself may have been defective. I chose your shop because of its excellent reputation, and I would like to keep recommending it to friends.

Would you be willing to replace the screen at cost, or at least to inspect the phone free of charge to find out what went wrong? I can bring it in any afternoon this week.

Sincerely,
Elena

I'm really sorry.

Amelia

For example, when I was in high school, many of my classmates decided to take extra science classes simply because their closest friends were planning to study engineering. Their parents had encouraged other subjects for years with little success. In addition, social media keeps friends connected around the clock, so peer opinions are present even at home. For these reasons, I think friends now shape teenagers' values more than families do.

Maya mentions that students sometimes discover new interests, and I would add another reason: these courses teach students how to communicate with people who think differently. In the workplace, engineers must explain their ideas to managers, clients, and designers who do not share their technical background. A philosophy or literature class trains students to build clear arguments and listen carefully to other perspectives. My cousin, who studied computer science, told me that a required public speaking course turned out to be the most useful class she took, because she now presents her projects every week. Therefore, I believe a few required courses outside one's field make graduates more effective professionals.

transcription.text: I would advise a new company to focus on one product, as Jasmine suggests. Kevin is right that relying on a single item involves risk, but I think spreading resources too thinly is an even bigger danger. Another reason for focusing is that it makes marketing much simpler and cheaper. When a company has one clear product, it can explain exactly what makes that product special in a single message. For instance, a small bakery near my home began by selling only one type of bread. Because people knew it as the place for that bread, lines formed every morning, and the owner did not need to pay for advertising. Two years later, the bakery added pastries, and customers tried them immediately because they already trusted the brand. A clear focus helps a new business build that kind of trust.

transcription.text: I believe reducing the amount of food students take is the more effective approach, and I agree with Ethan's point that preventing waste is better than managing it afterward. Sofia raises a good concern about student satisfaction, but smaller portions do not mean students must go hungry, since they can always return for a second serving. My additional reason is that composting and donation programs require a lot of ongoing effort. Someone has to collect, sort, and transport the leftovers, and that costs money and energy every single day. In contrast, removing trays is a one-time change. At my high school, the cafeteria switched to smaller plates, and the amount of food thrown away dropped noticeably within a few weeks. Students simply got used to taking less. For these reasons, I think limiting what students take would make a bigger difference.
